report.summary: Knorr-Bremse AG is a Munich-based German manufacturer of braking systems for rail and commercial vehicles. The company presents a moderate-to-high supplier risk profile driven by recurring safety-critical product recalls, a resolved antitrust no-poach settlement, and a credit rating downgrade indicating margin pressure. The most significant red flags are the 2024 and 2025 brake chamber recalls affecting thousands of bus units due to potential manufacturing defects and air leaks. Procurement buyers should enforce strict quality assurance agreements, verify recall remediation status for supplied parts, and monitor financial stability and compliance commitments.

facts.text: Knorr-Bremse Aktiengesellschaft is a German manufacturer of braking systems for rail and commercial vehicles headquartered in Munich, Germany, with an official website at knorr-bremse.com.
Nova Bus recalled approximately 2,090 ZF North America Knorr-Bremse 20/22-57 brake chambers, part number K038830N00, due to a potential manufacturing defect causing air leaks.
Bendix Commercial Vehicle Systems recalled approximately 1,672 Knorr-Bremse 22/24-57 brake chambers, part number K068622, due to potential air leaks from improper manufacturing.
NHTSA Part 573 Safety Recall Report 24V-559 covers Nova Bus vehicles with production dates JUL 06, 2020 - JUN 03, 2021, including brake-related components.

The U.S. Department of Justice reached a settlement with Knorr-Bremse AG and Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation enjoining them from entering into, maintaining, or enforcing no-poach agreements in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act.
Knorr-Bremse India Private Limited was listed as Respondent-Corporate Debtor in an NCLT order delivered on 19.04.2023.
S&P Global Ratings downgraded Knorr-Bremse AG and stated its EBITDA margin profile is not expected to return to above-average over the next 24 months.
Knorr-Bremse has committed to a long-term target of net zero emissions (Scopes 1 to 3) by 2050, with expanded climate targets validated by the Science Based Target initiative.

Knorr-Bremse criticized Russia sanctions imposed in 2014 and 2015, stating they have hurt Europe substantially.
